# Package validation

These checks target Unity 2022.3 and VRChat Avatars SDK 3.10.x. They test the standalone package without the original Gesture Manager installed.

## Static checks

Run `python -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -v` for distribution and publishing checks. The archive tests cover Unity-ignored names and their metadata, empty-folder extraction, orphan metadata rejection, source identity, and asset/license preservation. When PowerShell is installed, they also execute `Build-Package.ps1` to check shared filtering and propagation of validation failures; otherwise that entry-point check reports a skip.

Run `node .github/scripts/Validate-Package.cjs` with `--dependency-root` pointing to each installed `com.vrchat.base` and `com.vrchat.avatars` package. To also check coexistence GUID isolation against an original Gesture Manager checkout, pass `--original-root` with that checkout's path.

The validator checks assembly dependencies, asset metadata, GUID uniqueness, serialized references, resource lookups, and the native DLL hash/importer/license files. Missing historical references are reported separately when an original baseline is available; they are not counted as resolved.

Run `node .github/scripts/Validate-Localization.cjs` to compare all five language catalogs, check source-key coverage, placeholders, line breaks and rich-text tags, and reject misleading Chinese performance grades or an ambiguous HSV brightness label. English display corrections override the canonical source wording; untranslated English entries use that source directly. SDK/product names, parameter identifiers and standard technical terms can intentionally remain unchanged.

`node .github/scripts/Prune-ControllerOrphans.cjs` performs a dry run of controller graph reachability. `--apply` prunes orphan object blocks in the eight built-in controllers and their matching restore snapshots. It verifies that the retained objects are byte-for-byte unchanged and rejects missing local graph references. This cleanup was applied to the initial Pro baseline after checking that other package assets and source code did not reference the orphan subobjects.

For a read-only report of external controller references, run `node .github/scripts/Inspect-ControllerReferences.cjs --sdk-root <com.vrchat.avatars directory>`. Supply `--output <report.json>` only when a saved diagnostic report is needed.

## Unity integration checks

Use a disposable Unity avatar project with the target SDK and this package installed. Copy `UnityProChecks.cs`, `UnityProLocalizationChecks.cs`, `UnityProMotionChecks.cs`, `UnityProPlayChecks.cs`, `UnityProGraphChecks.cs`, `UnityProCameraChecks.cs`, `UnityProSimulationRenderChecks.cs`, `UnityProStatisticsChecks.cs`, `UnityProStatisticsLifecycleChecks.cs`, `UnityProFontChecks.cs`, and `UnityProValidation.asmdef` into its `Assets/Editor` folder. Do not copy these scripts into a user's working avatar project for batch testing.

Run Unity with `-batchmode -nographics -projectPath <fixture> -executeMethod UnityProChecks.Run -logFile <log>`. For actual Play Mode session checks and GPU-rendered camera images, use a second invocation with `-executeMethod UnityProPlayChecks.Run` and omit `-nographics`. These runners exit Unity themselves; do not add `-quit` to the Play runner. Rendered validation images are saved beneath the fixture's `Temp/GestureManagerProValidation/SimulationViews` folder.

The editor runner creates a temporary GUI context to check localized UI caches, resource ownership, native analyzer initialization and preservation of user names/parameter identities. It also checks game-simulation tool registration, the absence of an independent lip-sync entry, default-enabled microphone settings, explicit manager binding, radial-first initialization, shared radial/Inspector sessions, radial icons, live localized tool captions and the absence of standalone feature menus or a language Preferences page. The motion checks inject deterministic input. Play checks exercise session ownership, movement publication, stop/pause/unlink/failure cleanup and restoration. Temporary-ground checks verify the absence of rendering components and use real physics to verify immediate grounding, standing and walking parameters, jumping and landing, unsupported movement beyond the floor, reuse of existing scene ground, and cleanup after stop, pause, unlink, input/startup failure, floor loss and disposal. They also verify game simulation with microphone lip sync disabled or unavailable. When a Windows microphone is available, they start real recording, check muted monitoring, inject a PCM frame into the active native analyzer, and verify speech-state restoration and recording release on stop, pause and avatar loss; otherwise those recording checks report a skip. The graph checks initialize a valid generic avatar through the actual simulator connection path and eight default animation layers. They do not establish equivalence with client-side replacement of SDK locomotion proxies. These runners do not validate physical control input, spoken-phoneme recognition accuracy, VR hardware, humanoid body IK or visual layout.

The motion checks also cover reference-derived acceleration/deceleration, direction reversal, forward running with independent strafe speed, Scene Shift/Space/C/Z event ownership and one-shot actions, default jump impulse and explicit height overrides. Session checks preserve external VR/tracking/posture state and verify explicit pose ownership, callback-failure cleanup and synchronous stopping. Graph checks distinguish unchanged SDK zero-duration proxies from an explicitly authored, test-only time-varying clip; that clip is never installed as an avatar animation or proxy replacement.

Observer checks create two real SceneView windows in the disposable project, and test the existing-camera fallback with every Scene view closed. They cover the default fixed Scene camera, live follow toggles without catch-up, measured horizontal/vertical displacement, repeated-poll stability, manual rotation/zoom/pan, independent restoration per view, preservation of the original scene camera, projection settings, free observer cursor input and the three-view V cycle. Camera component checks preserve existing view enum values, leave supplied observer transforms/projection unchanged and keep the avatar visible while rendering in observer mode. These checks do not replace interactive camera/input verification.

The GitHub workflow builds an archive only. It does not replace Unity integration or hardware validation.

`UnityProLocalizationChecks` covers stable persisted enum values, native-language selector order, automatic script/region selection, forward/reverse switching across all five languages, cached radial captions, structured nested formats, and preservation of user names that contain punctuation, line breaks or text equal to a translated caption. It also checks the displayed SDK friend-parameter identifier, semantic mode labels and performance terminology. Only explicitly localized strings carry translation provenance; user-provided text is never recovered by matching translated sentences.

`UnityProFontChecks` opens Model Statistics and two independent fixture windows together and checks their shared language-specific font chains, synthetic weight configuration, language switching and root attachment cleanup. It checks representative Japanese, Korean and Traditional Chinese glyph availability when those system fonts are installed. The runtime tools use the inherited IMGUI theme. The font check generates a real multi-page CJK atlas with unused null capacity, checks resource stability over 200 updates, and verifies recovery after invalidating an owned material or active atlas page. Actual scrolling/window geometry, glyph rendering and Play Mode font transitions still require graphics-enabled checks; the synchronous editor assertions do not replace those checks.

The statistics checks compare all 31 metric values and PC/Mobile grades with the installed SDK calculator, including simulator components, complete Bounds, raw constraint depth, available size values and unknown-value ratings. They check component/asset state, SDK ignore-delegate preservation, separate before-processing and processed records, the 48-record session history, avatar identity filtering, stage selection and localized UI. Injected SDK event payloads test build-state correlation, actual build-platform identification and bundle-size reporting for the matching platform only; these are not a real SDK build or external-processor acceptance test. Play Mode observations use the first Editor update, while manual Play Mode scans remain a separate source.

Run `UnityProChecks.Run` once more without `-nographics` to exercise the non-readable help-icon regression. It discards a test texture's CPU pixels, copies it through the production helper, compares GPU-rendered color/alpha pixels, checks error logs and verifies source/render-target preservation. The headless invocation explicitly skips that GPU-only check.

The Play runner also creates an unsaved avatar in the disposable fixture and runs the real SDK preprocessing callback pipeline on entering Play Mode. A controlled test processor removes one cube: both platform histories must retain 24 triangles before processing and 12 afterwards, independently of simulator initialization. This tests callback timing, not NDMF, MA or AAO compatibility. An optional fixture-only APW reference DLL can expose the upstream `AvatarPerformanceInfo`, `PerformanceInfo` and `PerformanceRankComputer` unchanged inside `ReadOnlyStatsComparison.ApwAlgorithm`, preserving the upstream MIT notice. The runner compares all metrics and overall ratings against that calculator by reflection. Add `-apwReferenceRequired` to fail if the reference is absent; otherwise this comparison explicitly reports a skip. Do not include APW's window or preprocessing callback in the reference DLL, and do not distribute it with Pro.
